_comment: RAW ARM TEMPLATE MODULE (deliberately not Bicep).
Grants one Entra ID principal permission to USE a Microsoft.Web/connections
managed API connection at runtime. Logic Apps Standard workflows that
reference a managed API connection with authentication type
ManagedServiceIdentity authenticate to the connector runtime with the
workflow host's identity; that identity must hold an access policy on the
connection resource or every connector call fails with an authorization
error, even after interactive OAuth consent on the connection itself has
been completed.
Why ARM JSON instead of Bicep: Microsoft.Web/connections/accessPolicies has
no published Bicep type at ANY api-version (verified: both 2016-06-01 and
2018-07-01-preview report BCP081 'does not have types available'). Declaring
it in Bicep would therefore require suppressing BCP081, which this
repository does not do. Authoring the resource in an ARM JSON template that
Bicep consumes as a module keeps `az bicep build` genuinely warning-free
without hiding a diagnostic. This is the same 'raw ARM exception' pattern
documented in docs/architecture.md for resource types AVM does not cover.
Deployed as a separate module rather than inside api-connections.bicep
because the Logic App's system-assigned principal ID does not exist until
the Logic App site is deployed, which happens after the connection -- the
same ordering rationale as modules/storage-container-role-assignment.bicep.

metadata.description: Name of the existing Microsoft.Web/connections resource.
Azure region of the connection resource.
Entra ID tenant ID of the principal being granted access.
Object (principal) ID granted use of the connection. For Logic Apps Standard managed-connector authentication this is the Logic App SYSTEM-ASSIGNED identity.
